newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Q1 GDP shrank 1.33 pct vs year ago.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Q1 GDP shrank 1.33 pct vs year ago.

text.p: Colombia's gross domestic product (GDP) shrank 1.33 percent in the first quarter of this year compared with the same period of 1996, the National Statistics Department said Saturday.
Compared to the last quarter of 1996, when GDP dropped 0.4 percent, the fall in the first quarter this year is 1.09 percent.

The results confirmed those issued in May by the National Planning Department that Colombia plunged into recession, with two consecutive quarters of GDP growth, for the first time in more than 50 years.

Saturday's result by the statistics department is the official figure and is slightly worse than that estimated by the planning department which said the fall in GDP had been 1.22 percent compared to the first quarter of 1996.

The Statistics department said in a statement that the poor GDP performance was due to the uncertaintly sparked by the government's decision to introduce a number of austerity measures as part of an economic state of emergency declared in January. Those measures had to be revoked in March when the Constitutional Court declared the move illegal.

It also blamed the fall in GDP on the strengthening peso currency and the economic slowdown sparked by tougher measures against narco-trafficking, much of the proceeds of which have traditionally been laundered through legitimate business interests.
